aiWriteStates.meaning: Creates or edits a row whose status meaning is draft.
Creates a decision whose status meaning is proposed.
Moves a draft or proposed record to submitted and starts the approval cards, or sends a request such as a review request. A request, never an approval. Allowed only where Tool Policy says so.
Stores a fact the caller reports, such as a deployment or a change result. Never a decision. Stamped with the actor kind.
Stores an ID, a URL, a label and a last seen date for something another tool owns.

A configuration draft: a patch stored on a Configuration Draft row (C46), never in force. The Configuration Set Version (C02) is created only at activation, after a person accepts the configuration change decision.
The caller withdraws a record it created and that is not final.

aiRules: AI never approves. No tool approves, rejects, accepts, authorizes, sets a tier, moves a stage, activates configuration, assigns a role or deletes.
A governed record that an AI client creates starts as draft or proposed.

Submitted is a request act, never an approval. An AI client may submit only where the Tool Policy row says AI May Submit = yes for that subject kind. Submission only starts approval cards that people answer.
Facts an AI client reports are stored as reported, with the actor kind. Links store an ID, a URL, a label and a last seen date. Neither is a decision.
A configuration change from an AI client is a candidate draft only. A person accepts its decision on a card, then the engine activates it.
Max AI State on a Tool Policy row can only tighten these states, never widen them. The engine contract caps it.

Whatever the tool or route, the engine refuses these writes from an AI client, an agent identity or a pipeline: a decision status of accepted or rejected, any approval outcome, registration status registered, the current tier, the current stage, a new configuration set version, a configuration table row and a role binding.

notTools.insteadWhere: Approval cards in Outlook and Teams. The approval runner writes the outcome as the approval writer.

notTools.act: Set a tier, move a stage, mark a change standard
notTools.insteadWhere: An accepted decision of the right type. The engine applies a pre-approved standard change model.

notTools.why: Nobody activates by hand. Activation follows the accepted decision.
notTools.insteadWhere: Acceptance of the configuration change decision on an approval card.

notTools.act: Assign or remove a role, add a group member

notTools.why: Live configuration rows change only inside the activation operation.
notTools.insteadWhere: propose_configuration_change stores a draft. Activation follows the accepted decision.

notTools.why: Records are append-only where it matters. Others are retired or withdrawn.
notTools.insteadWhere: withdraw_record, record_deployment_correction, link_component with outcome retired, retire through configuration.

notTools.act: Write a wiki page, a work item or a pipeline
notTools.why: The product never writes into other tools (D-17, D-19).
notTools.insteadWhere: The person's AI client, through the Azure DevOps or GitHub MCP servers, as the person.

notTools.act: Import Microsoft's inventory on a schedule

notTools.why: That is the Dataverse MCP server's job on Dataverse (D-16).
notTools.insteadWhere: The Dataverse MCP server, under the same table rules.

relations.meaning: Any signed-in person, with or without a product role.
Any person who holds at least one product role.
A holder of an active owner role (C28) on the subject's application, through an accepted ownership decision.
A holder of an active technical owner role on the subject's application.
A holder of an active owner role on the application of the record the link belongs to.
The requester of the intake request.
The person whose leave is recorded, whatever their role.
An owner of an application the leaving person owns.
The requester or creator of the record.
A holder of the R or C letter for the decision type (C31).
The document owner on the Document Link (O19).
For evidence: a person who may write the record the evidence supports.
